key_insight: HVOF-sprayed Ni-20Cr+40TiC reduced oxidation weight gain by 95.71% relative to bare SA516 boiler steel during cyclic testing at 900°C.
engineering_relevance: This coating offers a promising route to protect SA516 boiler steel against high-temperature oxidation through reduced porosity and a dense protective oxide scale.
method: Apply Ni-20Cr, Ni-20Cr+40TiC, and Ni-20Cr+40TiN coatings by HVOF and plasma spraying.
Characterize microstructure and phases using XRD, SEM/EDS, and X-ray mapping.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports severe oxide spalling and cracking on bare steel, while HVOF Ni-20Cr+40TiC achieved the greatest weight-gain reduction among the tested coatings.
watch_item: Performance was demonstrated in laboratory air cycling; durability under service-specific boiler atmospheres and longer exposures remains to be established.
paper_title: Microstructure and high-temperature oxidation behaviour of HVOF and plasma sprayed Ni–Cr-based ceramic coatings on SA516 boiler steel
